terms.gloss: winged; as a noun, a bird, especially a large one
evidence: Verg. A. 1.394: aetheriā lāpsa plagā Jovis āles (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Ave, ecce avēs! Cūr caudās tam brevēs habent?
phrases.english: Grandpa, look, birds! Why do they have such short tails? (moulting peacocks)
phrases.source: Libellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium

phrases.english: Jove’s bird, swooping from the region of the sky

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 279.
Lewis & Short: ales
